solution.brief: Wasp_Connection From Direction takes geometry, center points, and direction curves to create sequentially-IDed WaspConnection objects for part aggregation.
solution.principle:
Wasp connections are defined by a plane at each face — the center point sets the origin and the direction curve sets the X-axis. Sequential input order determines connection IDs, which must match what Wasp_Rule references.

Related insight: Related insight: WaspConnection objects created by this component are passed as inputs to Wasp_Basic Part, which bundles them with geometry and a name string into a WaspPart object. The name string (not the connection IDs) is what Wasp_Rule uses to identify part types — connection IDs identify specific faces within a part.

Related insight: Related insight: Connection IDs assigned by this component are 0-based integers determined by sequential input order. Wasp_Rule references these 0-based indices — an off-by-one assumption (treating them as 1-based) silently breaks rule matching without any error.

Related insight: Related insight: The geometry, center points, and direction curves consumed by Wasp_Connection From Direction are typically referenced from a paired Rhino .3dm file via GH parameter components (Brep, Point, Curve params). The correct .3dm must be open in Rhino before the GH file solves — if it is not open, these references will be empty and the entire downstream part/connection/aggregation chain will fail silently.

intents: how do I set up wasp connections for a part
what inputs does Connection From Direction need
how are wasp connection IDs assigned
I need to define where parts attach to each other in wasp
symptoms: WaspConnection objects not appearing or wrongly IDed in Wasp_Rule
connections not aligning correctly on aggregated parts
unsure what geometry or points to feed into ConnDir

preconditions: Wasp plugin is installed in Grasshopper
Part geometry (Brep or Mesh) is available and referenced from Rhino
Connection face center points are prepared and positioned correctly
Direction curves/lines are drawn to indicate X-axis orientation for each connection plane
Wasp_Basic Part component is available to receive the same geometry and the connection outputs

evolution_history.changes: The new pattern clarifies the downstream consumer of WaspConnection objects (Wasp_Basic Part) and distinguishes the role of connection IDs (face-level) vs. the part name string (type-level) in rule matching — a precision distinction worth capturing here.
New pattern explicitly states '0-based connection indices' — this precision clarifies the sequential-ID behavior already described in this neighbor and prevents off-by-one errors.

The new pattern establishes that Wasp part geometry originates in a paired .3dm file referenced via Rhino params. This is a prerequisite that directly affects how inputs to Wasp_Connection From Direction are sourced, and users need to know this before setting up connections.
